He has sent down to you the Book [meaning: the Qur'an] with truth [meaning: with truthfulness in its reports], confirming what is before it [meaning: agreeing with what was foretold of it in the other scriptures], and He sent down the Torah and the Gospel.

﴿Before (this), as guidance for the people, and He sent down the Criterion﴾ (al-Furqan), that by which truth is distinguished from falsehood, meaning: all the books that He sent down. ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah will have a severe punishment. And Allah is Mighty, Owner of Retribution﴾ — Owner of punishment.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 6:

﴿He is the One who forms you﴾ He makes you into forms in the wombs of your mothers ﴿as He wills﴾ male and female, short and tall, black and white.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 7:

﴿He it is who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are clear (muhkamat)﴾. These are the three verses at the end of Surah al-An'am: ﴿Say: "Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you"﴾ up to the end of the three verses. ﴿They are the mother of the Book﴾: they are the mother of every book that Allah the Exalted sent down to every prophet. In them is everything that He made lawful and unlawful. Its meaning is that they are the foundation of the Book upon which action is based. ﴿And others﴾ means: other verses ﴿that are unclear (mutashabihat)﴾. He means: those that were confused for the Jews, and these are the disjointed letters (huruf al-tahajji) at the beginnings of the surahs. This is because they interpreted them by the reckoning of the abjad (hisab al-jummal) and sought to extract from them the duration of this community's existence, so it became confused and ambiguous for them. ﴿As for those in whose hearts is deviation﴾ are the Jews who sought knowledge of the term of this community from the disjointed letters. ﴿They follow what is unclear of it﴾ of the Book, meaning: the disjointed letters. ﴿Seeking discord﴾: seeking confusion so that they might mislead their ignorant ones with it. ﴿And seeking its interpretation﴾: seeking the term of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And none knows its interpretation except Allah﴾: meaning, none knows the end of the dominion of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) except Allah, because the end of their dominion coincides with the Hour, and no one knows that except Allah. Then He began and said: ﴿And those firmly grounded in knowledge﴾, that is, those firm in it, meaning: the scholars among the believers of the People of the Book. ﴿Say: "We believe in it"﴾, that is, in the unclear, ﴿all of it is from our Lord﴾: the clear and the unclear, what we know and what we do not know. ﴿And none will be reminded except those of understanding (ulu al-albab)﴾: none is admonished by the Qur'an except those possessed of intellect.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 8:

﴿Our Lord﴾ meaning: and those firm in knowledge say, ﴿"Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us"﴾ do not incline them away from guidance and rectitude, as You have caused the hearts of those in whose hearts is deviation to deviate, ﴿after You have guided us﴾ to faith in the muhkam (clear, unambiguous verses) and the mutashabih (allegorical, ambiguous verses) of Your Book.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 9:

﴿Our Lord, You are gathering the people﴾ (meaning: gathering them) ﴿for a Day﴾ (meaning: of recompense), on a day ﴿about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in the promise﴾ (meaning: of resurrection and recompense).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 10:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾ meaning: the Jews of Qurayzah and al-Nadir. ﴿Their wealth will not avail them﴾ that is: will not benefit them and will not ward off from them ﴿nor their children﴾ meaning: the things in which they take pride ﴿against Allah﴾ against the punishment of Allah ﴿at all. And they are the fuel of the Fire﴾ they are those by whom the Fire will be kindled.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 11:

﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾: like the practice and conduct of the people of Pharaoh in disbelief and denial. The Jews disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ).

Say to those who disbelieved, "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place" (Surah Al 'Imran 3:12). That is, the Jews of Madinah and the polytheists of Makkah. "Wretched is the resting place": evil is what has been prepared for you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 13:

﴿There has indeed been a sign for you﴾, a sign that shows the truthfulness of Muhammad (peace be upon him), ﴿in the two hosts﴾, meaning the Muslims and the polytheists, ﴿that met﴾, that came together on the day of Badr for battle. ﴿One host fighting in the way of Allah﴾, and they are the Muslims, ﴿and another disbelieving, seeing them twice their number﴾, and they were three times their number, but Allah the Exalted made them seem few in their eyes and showed them [the Muslims a number] according to what He had informed them, that they would overcome them, so that their hearts would be strengthened. This is because Allah the Mighty and Majestic had informed the Muslims that a hundred of them would overcome two hundred of the disbelievers. ﴿With their own eyes﴾, that is, from where the sight falls on them. ﴿And Allah supports﴾, strengthens ﴿with His help﴾, with victory and proof, ﴿whom He wills﴾. ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson﴾, and it is the sign by which one passes from the station of ignorance to knowledge, ﴿for those who have insight﴾, for those who possess understanding.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 14:

﴿Adorned for people is the love of desires﴾ — plural of shahwah (desire), which is the soul's longing for a thing. ﴿And the heaped-up piles of gold and silver﴾ — abundant wealth gathered together. ﴿And the branded horses﴾ — grazing (ra'iyah); it is also said: trained (mu'allamah), like the piebald and those with markings (dhawat al-shiyat); it is also said: the beautiful ones. And "al-khayl" (horses) means mares. ﴿And the cattle﴾ — camels, cows and sheep. ﴿And the tilth﴾ — that which is sown and planted. Then he made clear that these things are the enjoyment of this world, and they are perishing and transient. ﴿And with Allah is the best return﴾ — the place of return. Then he informed that better than all of that is what He has prepared for His friends, so He said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 15:

﴿Say, "Shall I inform you of something better than that?" For those who fear Allah [from associating partners with Him] are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally, and purified spouses, and approval from Allah. And Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.﴾

﴿The patient﴾ in their religion and in what befalls them, ﴿the truthful﴾ in their intentions, ﴿the devout﴾ who obey God, ﴿those who spend﴾ from what is lawful in obedience to God, ﴿and those who seek forgiveness at the dawn hours﴾, meaning those who pray the dawn prayer. It is said: it was revealed concerning the Emigrants (muhajirun) and the Helpers (ansar).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 18:

﴿Allah bears witness﴾ — He made clear and manifest, by the proofs He has set up, ﴿that there is no god except Him, and the angels﴾ — that is, the angels also bear witness, meaning: they affirm the Oneness of Allah. ﴿And those of knowledge﴾ — they are the Prophets and the scholars among the believers of the People of the Book and the Muslims. ﴿Standing in justice﴾ — that is, standing upon justice, directing the management of all affairs with uprightness.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 19:

﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam.﴾ The polytheists boasted of their religions, and each group said: "There is no religion except ours, and it is the religion of Allah." So this verse was revealed, and Allah, exalted is He, refuted them, saying: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾ — the one brought by Muhammad (peace be upon him). ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not differ﴾ — i.e., the Jews did not differ regarding the truthfulness of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), since they found it in their Book. ﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾ — meaning: the Prophet (ﷺ). He was called "knowledge" because he was known to them by his description and attributes before his mission. When he came to them, they differed concerning him: some of them believed in him, and others disbelieved. ﴿out of jealousy among themselves⁠﻿﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿⁠—﻿﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿⁠﻿⁠﻿﻿⁠﻿﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ ⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿⁠﻿⁠﻿﻿ ⁠ (bagyan baynahum)﻿﻿﻿﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿⁠﻿⁠﻿⁠ ⁠﻿﻿﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿ ⁠﻿⁠ ⁠ ⁠﻿﻿⁠ ⁠⁠ —﻿⁠ ﻿﻿ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠﻿﻿⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿⁠ ⁠ ⁠﻿﻿﻿ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠ ⁠

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 20:

﴿Then if they argue with you﴾ meaning: they dispute with you. ﴿Then say: "I have submitted my face to God"﴾ meaning: I have made my deeds sincere for God and surrendered to Him. ﴿And those who follow me﴾ meaning: the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun) and the Helpers (al-Ansar). ﴿And say to those who were given the Book and to the unlettered: "Have you submitted?"﴾ meaning: the Arabs. "Have you submitted?" is a question whose meaning is a command, i.e., "Submit!" And His words ﴿Your duty is only to convey (al-balagh)﴾ meaning: the conveying (al-tabligh), and it is not your duty to guide them. ﴿And God is seeing of [His] servants﴾ meaning: He sees those who believed in you and affirmed you, and those who disbelieved in you and denied you. This was before he was commanded to fight.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 21:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right﴾. Its explanation has already passed in Surah al-Baqarah. And [His statement]: ﴿and kill those who enjoin justice from among the people﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Children of Israel killed forty-three prophets at the beginning of the day, in a single hour. Then there arose one hundred and twelve men from among the worshippers of the Children of Israel, who enjoined upon those who were killing them what is good and forbade them from what is evil, and they were all killed by the end of that same day. They are the ones whom Allah mentioned in this verse." And these who were in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) were loyal to them, so they are included among them.

Those are the ones whose deeds have been nullified (حبطت), that is, their deeds which they claim (من التمسك بالتوراة وإقامة شرع موسى) to be adherence to the Torah and upholding the law of Moses, peace be upon him, are void ﴿in this world﴾, because they did not safeguard their blood and their property, ﴿and﴾ in ﴿the Hereafter﴾, because they did not deserve any reward for them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 23:

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture?﴾ He means: the Jews. ﴿They are called to the Book of Allah so that it may judge between them.﴾ This was because they denied the verse of stoning (al-rajm) in the Torah, and they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the punishment for married persons (al-muhsanin) if they committed adultery. He judged for stoning, so they said: "You have deviated, O Muhammad." He said: "Between me and you is the Torah." Then they brought Ibn Suriya al-A'war, and he read the Torah. When he reached the verse of stoning, he covered it with his palm. Then Ibn Salam stood up, lifted his hand from it, and read it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to the Jews. The Jews became extremely angry at that and dispersed. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿Then a faction of them turn away, while they are averse.﴾ He means: the scholars and the leaders.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 24:

﴿That﴾ means: that turning away from your judgment is due to their delusion, when they said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days,﴾ and ﴿what they used to fabricate deluded them in their religion﴾ — their fabrication, which is their saying: ﴿The Fire will not touch us.﴾ This has already been discussed in Surat al-Baqarah.

﴿So how will it be when We gather them﴾ means: how will their condition be when We gather them ﴿for﴾ the recompense of ﴿a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be paid in full for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged﴾, by having their good deeds diminished or their evil deeds increased.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 26:

﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty﴾. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah and promised his community the kingdoms of Persia and Rome, the hypocrites and the Jews said: "Far-fetched, far-fetched! (Persia and Rome are too mighty and too well-protected to be overcome in their lands)." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse, and His words: ﴿You give sovereignty to whom You will﴾, namely Muhammad and his companions, ﴿and You take sovereignty away from whom You will﴾, namely Abu Jahl and the chieftains of Quraysh, ﴿You honour whom You will﴾, namely the Emigrants and the Helpers, ﴿and You abase whom You will﴾, namely Abu Jahl and his companions, until their heads were cut off and they were thrown into the well. ﴿In Your hand is all good﴾, that is, the honour of this world and the Hereafter. He intended "good and evil," but he sufficed with mentioning "good" because the desire for it is in doing good to the servant, not evil.

﴿You cause the night to enter the day﴾, meaning You make what is lost from one of them an increase in the other. ﴿And You bring the living out of the dead, and You bring the dead out of the living﴾: You bring the animal out of the sperm-drop, and You bring the sperm-drop out of the animal, and You bring the believer out of the disbeliever and the disbeliever out of the believer. ﴿And You provide for whom You will without account﴾, without restriction or constriction.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 28:

﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies (awliya') instead of the believers﴾, that is: helpers and supporters, from among other than the believers. It was revealed concerning a group of believers who used to have secret dealings with the Jews (that is, they would be intimate with them) and show them loyalty. ﴿And whoever does that﴾, taking them as allies, ﴿then he has nothing whatsoever with Allah﴾, that is: nothing of the religion of Allah, meaning he has disassociated himself from Allah and departed from His religion. Then he made an exception, saying: ﴿except when you fear a danger from them﴾, that is, taqiyya (dissimulation for protection). This applies to the believer when he is among disbelieving people and fears for his property and his life; then he may oppose them outwardly and be courteous to them with his tongue while his heart remains at peace with faith, as a means of protecting himself. Ibn 'Abbas said: he means outward courtesy. ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾, that is: Allah frightens you regarding the allying with disbelievers with the punishment of Himself (he means: His punishment, and He singled it out by attributing it to Himself as a glorification of it). So when He forbade that, He warned and cautioned against secretly holding allegiance to them, and said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 29:

﴿Say: Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it,﴾ meaning what is in your inner selves regarding taking them as allies or abandoning them, ﴿Allah knows it, and He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth.﴾ This completes the warning, for if nothing in them is hidden from Him, how could the inner intention be hidden from Him? ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent.﴾ A warning of the punishment of One whom nothing can overpower.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 30:

﴿The day every soul finds what it has done of good brought forward﴾. That is: "And Allah warns you of His own punishment." "The day" means: that day. And His saying ﴿what it has done of good brought forward﴾ means: the recompense for what it did, in the form of the reward you see. ﴿And what it has done of evil, it wishes that between it and that there were a great distance﴾: an extreme distance, as the distance between the east and the west.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 31:

﴿Say﴾, i.e., to the disbelievers, ﴿If you truly love Allah﴾ [The Prophet ﷺ stood over the Quraysh while they were prostrating to idols, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah, you have opposed the religion of your father Ibrahim." The Quraysh said: "We only worship these out of love for Allah, so that they may bring us closer to Allah."] So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿If you truly love Allah﴾, and worship idols so that they may bring you closer to Him, ﴿then follow me, and Allah will love you﴾. For I am His Messenger to you and His proof against you. The meaning of the servant's love for Allah, glory be to Him, is his desire to obey Him and his preference for His command. The meaning of Allah's love for the servant is His desire to reward him, to pardon him, and to bestow His favour upon him.
﴿Say, "Obey Allah and the Messenger."﴾ But if they turn away from obedience, ﴿then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾, meaning He does not forgive them nor praise them.

ﷻ

﴿Indeed, God chose Adam﴾ by prophethood and messengerhood, ﴿and Noah, and the family of Abraham﴾, meaning Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes (al-Asbat), ﴿and the family of ʿImran﴾, meaning Moses and Aaron, ﴿above the worlds﴾, above the worlds of their own times.

Dhurriyyatan (ذريةً): meaning He chose a progeny, **"bA'DUHA min ba'ḍ"** (بعضها من بعض), i.e., from the offspring of one another, because all of them are the progeny of Adam, then the progeny of Nuh. **"Wa-Allahu samee'"** (﴿والله سميع﴾): He hears what the chosen progeny say; **"'aleem"** (﴿عليمٌ﴾): He knows what they conceal, and for this reason He preferred them over others.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 35:

﴿When the wife of ʿImrān said: "My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering"﴾. She was Ḥannah, the mother of Maryam. ﴿Indeed, I have vowed to You what is in my womb﴾, meaning: I made it obligatory upon myself to dedicate what is in my womb ﴿as a dedicated offering﴾, freed (ʿatīq), purely for God, a servant of the church, devoted to worship and to serving the church. It was obligatory upon their children to obey them in their vows. So she gave her child in charity to Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy House, Jerusalem).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 36:

﴿So when she delivered her, she said, "My Lord, I have delivered a female," - and the male is not like the female.﴾ She apologized for what she had done in vowing (her child), when she gave birth to a female. ﴿And the male is not like the female﴾ in serving the church, because of what befalls her of menstruation and postnatal bleeding. ﴿And I seek refuge for her in You﴾ i.e., I protect her and grant her refuge ﴿from Satan, the accursed﴾, the cursed, the expelled.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 37:

﴿So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance﴾, that is, He was pleased with her in place of the freed child that she had been vowed, ﴿and caused her to grow in a good growth﴾ in righteousness, chastity, knowledge of God, and obedience to Him. ﴿And Zakariyya took charge of her﴾, undertaking the care of her affairs. He built for her a niche (mihrab) in the mosque, which could not be reached except by a ladder. The mihrab (miḥrāb) is the upper chamber, and this is His saying: ﴿Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the mihrab, he found provision with her﴾, that is, winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter, which the angels brought her from Paradise. When Zakariyya saw what Maryam had been given of (summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer), contrary to the usual course of things, he longed for a child from a barren wife, contrary to the usual course of things, and that is His saying:

﴿Hunalika﴾, that is, at that time, ﴿Zakariyya called upon his Lord﴾, [saying] ﴿He said: My Lord, grant me from Yourself﴾, that is, from Your presence, ﴿good offspring﴾, that is, a blessed, pious progeny. So God answered his supplication and sent the angels to him bearing good news, and this is His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 39:

﴿Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: "Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah"﴾ That is: confirming Isa, that he is the Spirit of Allah and His word. Isa was called "the word of Allah" because he came into being at the saying ﴿"Be"﴾, so the name "word" was applied to him because it was by it that he came to be. ﴿And a leader﴾ and noble before his Lord, ﴿and chaste﴾, and this is the one who does not approach women and has no desire for them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 40:

﴿He said﴾ — Zakariyya, when he was given the good news of a son: ﴿"My Lord, how can I have a son?"﴾ That is: in what state will that be? Will You return me to the state of youth while my wife is as she is, or will it be with the state of old age? ﴿And old age has indeed overtaken me﴾ That is: I have reached it, for on that day he was a hundred and twenty years old. ﴿And my wife is barren﴾ unable to bear children, and she was ninety-eight years old. He was told: ﴿"Thus"﴾ That is: such is the matter, namely the granting of a child in old age; ﴿Allah does what He wills﴾. So glory be to He for whom nothing is too difficult. Then, when he was given the good news of a son, he asked Allah for a sign by which he would know the time of his wife's conception, and that is His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 41:

﴿Qāla rabbi ijʿal lī āyah﴾ (He said, "My Lord, appoint for me a sign"). Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days﴾. Allah the Exalted made the sign of his wife's pregnancy that his tongue would be restrained, so that he would not be able to speak to the people for three days ﴿except by gesture﴾, that is, by signaling with the lips, the eyebrows and the eyes. Yet he was still able to glorify God and remember Him, and this is His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord much and glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning﴾, that is, and pray (wa-ṣalli, ﴿wa-sabbiḥ﴾ being understood here as prayer). ﴿In the evening﴾ is the last part of the day, and ﴿the morning﴾ is what lies between the break of dawn and the forenoon (ḍuḥā).

Translation:

﴿And when the angels said﴾ meaning: Gabriel alone, peace be upon him: ﴿O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you﴾ meaning: by favouring you with such grace that you devoted yourself entirely to His obedience ﴿and purified you﴾ from the touch of men and from menstruation ﴿and chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾ above the women of the worlds of your time.

﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord.﴾ Stand for the prayer (al-ṣalāh) before your Lord. So she stood until her feet swelled and oozed pus. ﴿And prostrate yourself and bow down.﴾ That is: come with the bowing (rukūʿ) and the prostration (sujūd). The conjunction "wa" (و) does not require sequence. ﴿Along with those who bow.﴾ That is: do as they do. He said ﴿with those who bow﴾ and did not say "with the women who bow" because the masculine form is more general.

That is, what We have related to you of the story of Zakariya and Maryam is ﴿from the news of the unseen﴾, that is, from its reports, ﴿which We reveal to you﴾, that is, which We send down to you, ﴿and you were not with them﴾ so that you would know it, ﴿when they cast their pens﴾. This is because when Hannah gave birth to Maryam, she brought her to the custodians of the Temple of Jerusalem and said to them: "Take this consecrated child." The rabbis competed for her until they drew lots over her, and the lot fell to Zakariya. That is His saying: ﴿when they cast their pens﴾, that is, their arrows (qidah) with which they drew lots, to see which of them would be entitled to the guardianship (kafalah) of Maryam.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 45:

﴿When the angels said⁠﴾ meaning: Jibril (peace be upon him): ﴿O Maryam, Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him⁠﴾ meaning: ʿIsa (peace be upon him), because at the beginning of his affair he was a word from Allah, and he came into being by a word from Him, that is, from Allah. ﴿His name will be the Messiah⁠﴾ — it is an Arabicized form of Mashiha in Syriac, a title for ʿIsa. Then he explained and clarified who he is, saying: ﴿ʿIsa son of Maryam, distinguished⁠﴾ meaning: possessing standing, honour and rank ﴿in this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near⁠﴾ to the reward of Allah and His honour.

Translation:

﴿And he will speak to the people in the cradle﴾ as a child, ﴿and in maturity﴾ meaning: he will speak with prophethood in maturity. It was also said: after his descent from the heaven. ﴿And he will be among the righteous﴾ meaning: like Musa (Moses), Ya'qub (Jacob), Ishaq (Isaac) and Ibrahim (Abraham), peace be upon them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 47:

﴿Maryam said﴾ in amazement: ﴿"How can I have a child when no man has touched me?"﴾ ﴿He said: "So it is; God creates what He wills"﴾, that is, like this kind of thing, which is the creation of a child without a man touching her. That is, the matter is as you say, but God ﴿when He decrees a matter, says to it only "Be," and it is﴾. This was mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah (to its end).
﴿And He will teach him the Book﴾. He meant: writing and penmanship.

And [He will make him] a messenger to the Children of Israel, [saying]: "Indeed I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, [which is that] I create for you from clay [something] like the form of a bird, and I breathe into it, and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission. And I heal the one born blind (al-akmah), and the leper (al-abras), [meaning] the one who has baraṣ, that is, whiteness [on the skin]. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store (tadkharun) for the rest of your day."

﴿And confirming﴾ i.e., I have come to you confirming ﴿what is before me﴾, i.e., the Scripture that was revealed before me, ﴿and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you﴾. He made lawful for them, through the tongue of the Messiah, the flesh of camels, the fat (al-thurub, the fat covering the entrails), and some kinds of birds and fish, which had been forbidden in the law of Musa (Moses), peace be upon him. ﴿And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord﴾, i.e., the miracles he had with him that indicate his prophethood. He used the singular (āyah) because they are all one kind in their indication (of his prophethood).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 52:

﴿Then when Jesus perceived disbelief from them﴾ he knew and saw it, ﴿and that was because they intended to kill him when he invited them to God, Exalted is He, so he sought help against them. And he said: "Who are my helpers toward God?"﴾ That is: with God and for the sake of God. ﴿The disciples (al-Hawariyyun) said﴾ — and they were fullers (qassarin) who whiten (yuhawwirun) garments, that is, they bleach them — "They believed in Jesus and followed him: ﴿We are the helpers of God﴾, the helpers of His religion. ﴿We believe in God, so bear witness﴾ O Jesus, ﴿that we are Muslims.﴾"

Here is the translation:

And His saying: ﴿So write us down among the witnesses﴾, meaning: with those who bore witness to the prophets to their truthfulness. The meaning is: record our names alongside theirs, so that we may attain the same success they attained.

[Qur'anic quotations are in ﴿ ﴾ markers.]

﴿And they schemed﴾, meaning they strove to kill him by deceit. ﴿And Allah schemed﴾, meaning He recompensed them for their scheming by casting the likeness of Jesus upon the one who pointed him out, so that he was seized and crucified. ﴿And Allah is the best of schemers﴾, meaning the best of those who requite, for the requital of an evil deed is punishment, since no one is more able to do that than Him.

﴿When God said: "O Jesus"﴾. The meaning is: "And [God] plotted, when God said: 'O Jesus, I am causing you to die'", that is: "I am taking you in full, without death." Meaning: they will not be able to harm you in any way. ﴿And raising you to Myself﴾, that is: to My heaven and the place of My honour. He described that as "raising to Him" for exaltation and magnification, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord﴾ (37:99), and he [Abraham] only went to Syria, while the meaning is: to the command of my Lord. ﴿And purifying you from those who disbelieve﴾, that is: removing you from among them. ﴿And making those who follow you﴾, and they are the people of Islam from this nation who followed the religion of the Messiah and affirmed him as the messenger of God, for by God, none who called him a lord followed him, ﴿above those who disbelieve﴾ in proof, argument, honour and victory.

This is a translation of the passage as given, with the Qur'anic quotations rendered in the ﴿ ﴾ markers.

﴿That﴾ means: what has preceded of the account concerning Jesus and Mary, peace be upon them both. ﴿We recite it to you﴾: we inform you of it. ﴿From the signs﴾: that is, the indications that point to your prophethood, because they are reports of matters which you did not witness and did not read in any book. ﴿And the Wise Reminder﴾: that is, the Qur'an, which is muhkam (firmly established, protected) from falsehood. It was also said: "al-Hakim" means "the one who judges," in the sense of "the one who prevents" disbelief and corruption.

The verse 3:59 was revealed concerning the delegation of Najran when they said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Have you seen a child without a father?" So God, exalted is He, argued against them with Adam, peace be upon him. That is: the analogy of the creation of Isa, peace be upon him, without a father is like the analogy of the creation of Adam, peace be upon him. Rather, the matter in it is astonishing, for he was created without a father and without a mother.

His saying ﴿عند الله﴾ ("with God") means: in the bringing into being and the creation. The sentence is complete at His saying ﴿كمثل آدم﴾ ("like Adam"). Then He began another report from the story of Adam, peace be upon him, so He said: ﴿خلقه من تراب﴾ ("He created him from dust"), that is: as a form of clay from dust. ﴿ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ كُنْ﴾ ("then He said to him: Be"), a human being, ﴿فَيَكُونُ﴾ ("and he was"), in the sense of فكان (fa-kāna, "so he was").

The truth is from your Lord. That is, the account I have told you about Jesus is the truth from your Lord. ﴿So do not be among the doubters.﴾ That is, among those who doubt. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and what is meant is a prohibition to others against doubt.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 61:

﴿Whoever argues with you﴾ disputes with you ﴿concerning it﴾ concerning Jesus ﴿after the knowledge has come to you﴾ that Jesus is the servant of Allah and His messenger ﴿then say: "Come, let us call"﴾ come on, let us summon ﴿our sons and your sons﴾ When Allah, exalted is He, argued against the Christians by way of analogy with His words: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus in the sight of Allah﴾ to the end of the verse, the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to argue against them by way of the miraculous. So when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invited the delegation of Najran to mubahalah (mutual imprecation, a solemn call for Allah's curse upon the liar among the two parties). It is the supplication against the wrongdoer from either of the two parties. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out with al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Ali and Fatimah, peace be upon them, and he said to them: "When I supplicate, say Amin." That is His words: ﴿our sons﴾ to the end of the verse. And His words: ﴿and our women and your women﴾ meaning: and our close kin ﴿then let us earnestly pray﴾ let us humbly supplicate in prayer. It has been said: we invoke with the mubahalah, which is the curse, so we call upon Allah with the curse against the liars. The Christians did not agree to the mubahalah out of fear of the curse, and they accepted the jizyah (poll tax).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 62:

﴿Indeed, this﴾ that We have revealed to you ﴿is the true narrative﴾, the truthful report.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 63:

﴿Then if they turn away﴾ — they turn away from what you have brought of clarification — ﴿then indeed Allah﴾ knows who among His creation is corrupt, and He will requite him for that.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 64:

﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you"﴾ — meaning: the Jews of Madinah and the Christians of Najran. ﴿A word﴾ means: a statement containing the explanation of a matter. ﴿Equitable﴾ means: just, ﴿between us and you﴾. Then he explained the word, saying: ﴿that we not worship except Allah, and not associate anything with Him﴾ — that is, we do not worship anything alongside Him besides Him. ﴿And that some of us do not take others as lords besides Allah﴾ — as the Christians took ʿĪsā (ʿalayhi al-salām) and the Children of Israel took ʿUzayr. It was also said: it means we do not obey anyone in disobedience to Allah, as Allah said describing them when they obeyed their scholars in disobeying Him: ﴿They took their rabbis﴾ (the verse). ﴿But if they turn away﴾ — they refuse to respond — ﴿then say: "Bear witness that we are Muslims"﴾ — affirming monotheism (tawhid).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 65:

﴿O People of the Book, why do you argue about Abraham?﴾ It was revealed when the Jews and the Christians disputed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about Abraham (peace be upon him). The Jews said: "Abraham was none other than a Jew," and the Christians said: "He was none other than a Christian." As for His saying: ﴿And the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him﴾, that means: Judaism and Christianity came into being after the revelation of the two Books, whereas the two Books were revealed a long time after his death. ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾ (i.e., to recognize) the falsity of this claim.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 66:

﴿Ha antum﴾ meaning: you are ﴿these﴾, meaning: O you ﴿argued﴾, that is, disputed and contended ﴿about what you have knowledge of﴾, meaning: what they found in their books, and whose explanation and story were revealed to them. ﴿Why then do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge?﴾ concerning the affair of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and your book does not state that he was a Jew or a Christian. ﴿But Allah knows﴾ the affair of Ibrahim, ﴿and you know not.﴾ Then He clarified his condition, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 67:

﴿Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a ḥanīf (upright, one who turns away from falsehood), a Muslim (one who submits)﴾ and the verse [continues]. Then he made the Muslims the most entitled of people to him, and said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 68:

﴿Indeed, the closest of people to Abraham﴾ means: the nearest of them to him and the most entitled to him, ﴿are those who followed him﴾ in his religion and creed, ﴿and this Prophet﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿and those who believe﴾, meaning: they are the ones who should say, "We are upon the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 69:

﴿A group of the People of the Book wish they could lead you astray﴾ The Jews wanted to cause the Muslims to slip from their religion and return them to disbelief, so this verse was revealed: ﴿Yet they lead astray none but themselves﴾, because the believers do not accept their words, so the sin falls upon them for their wishing to mislead the believers. ﴿And they do not perceive﴾ that this harms them and does not harm the believers.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 70:

﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿while you witness﴾ to what indicates its truth from your own scripture, because in it is the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and mention of him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 71:

﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you mix [truth with falsehood]﴾ It is mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 72:

﴿And a group of the People of the Book said﴾ That is, a number of the Jews said to one another: "Display belief in Muhammad and the Qur'an at the beginning of the day, and turn back from it at the end of the day, for that is more likely to make his companions turn away from his religion and doubt, when you say: 'We examined your scripture and found that Muhammad is not that one.'" So Allah informed His Prophet, peace be upon him, of the secret of the Jews and their scheming through this verse.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 73:

﴿And do not believe﴾ This is a report of the speech of the Jews to one another. They said: Do not affirm, nor acknowledge, that ﴿anyone should be given the like of what you have been given﴾ of knowledge, wisdom, the Book, proof, the manna and the quail, virtues and honours; ﴿except for him who follows your religion﴾, Judaism, and performs its laws. As for His words: ﴿Say: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of Allah﴾, it is a parenthetical interjection between the object and its verb, and it is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, not from the speech of the Jews. Its meaning: indeed, the religion is the religion of Allah. As for His words: ﴿or they will argue with you before your Lord﴾, it is coordinated with His words: ﴿that anyone should be given﴾, and the meaning is: do not believe that they will argue with you before your Lord, because you are more correct in religion than they are, so they will have no proof against you. Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Indeed, bounty is in the hand of Allah﴾, meaning: what Allah has bestowed upon you and upon your community.

ﷺ-free passage; no hadith. Translate faithfully.

﴿Specifies with His mercy﴾ with His religion, Islam, ﴿whomever He wills. And God is the possessor of great bounty﴾ upon His allies, ﴿the Mighty﴾, because nothing is greater with God than Islam. Then He informed about the difference in their conditions regarding trustworthiness and treachery, with His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 75:

﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you.﴾ He means: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam was entrusted with twelve hundred ounces of gold, and he returned the trust to the one who had entrusted him.

﴿And among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you﴾ He means: Finhas ibn ʿAzuraʾ (Finhas ibn ʿAzura) was entrusted with a dinar and betrayed it.

﴿Unless you keep standing over him﴾ at his head, staying in his company. If you give him respite and delay him, he denies [it]. ﴿That﴾ i.e., the considering of it lawful and the betrayal. ﴿Because they﴾ say: ﴿There is no blame upon us﴾ regarding what we have taken from the wealth of the Arabs, because they are polytheists. So "the unlettered ones" (al-ummiyyun) in this verse are all the Arabs. Then God, exalted, denied them in this, saying: ﴿And they speak falsehood against God﴾, because they claimed that this was in their Book, and they lied, for the trust is to be fulfilled in every sacred law. ﴿And they know﴾ that they are lying. Then He answered their statement: ﴿There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered ones.﴾ by His saying:

"Yes" — rather, "Yes, there is a way (against them in that)." Then he began, saying: ﴿Whoever fulfils his covenant﴾, meaning: the covenant of God that He made with him in the Torah, of believing in Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Qur'an, and who renders the trust, and guards against disbelief, treachery and breaking the covenant — ﴿then indeed God loves the God-fearing (al-muttaqun)﴾, meaning: whoever has this description.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 77:

﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah﴾ It was revealed concerning two men who brought a dispute before the Prophet (ﷺ) over a piece of land. The defendant intended to swear an oath, so this verse was revealed, and the defendant refrained from the oath and acknowledged the truth. The meaning of ﴿sell﴾ (yashtaruna) is "exchange" (yastabdiluna), ﴿the covenant of Allah﴾ refers to His commandment to the believers that they not swear falsely by His name, ﴿and their oaths﴾ refers to all oaths, namely swearing, ﴿for a little price﴾ of this worldly life. ﴿They shall have no share in the Hereafter﴾, meaning: they shall have no portion in it. ﴿Allah will not speak to them﴾ with words that would please them, ﴿nor look at them﴾ with mercy. Most of the exegetes hold that the verse was revealed concerning the Jews and their concealment of the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ), and their faith which they exchanged, which is the truth in the Torah concerning the description of Muhammad (peace be upon him). The proof of the correctness of this is his saying:

And indeed among them ﴿is﴾, that is, among the Jews, a group who twist their tongues with the Book, distorting it by alteration and substitution. The meaning: they twist their tongues away from the course of what is right, by what they bring from their own selves, ﴿so that you may think it to be﴾, that is, so that you may think what they twist with their tongues ﴿to be from the Book﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 79:

﴿It is not for a human﴾ ... When the Jews claimed that they were upon the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and Allah the Exalted refuted them, they became angry and said: "What would please you from us, O Muhammad, except that we take you as a lord?" [The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I seek refuge in Allah that we should command the worship of other than Allah."] And this verse was revealed: ﴿It is not for a human being that he should be given the Book and wisdom and prophethood and then say to the people, "Be worshippers of me rather than Allah"﴾ ... that he should combine these two: prophethood and calling the creation to the worship of other than Allah. ﴿But [rather he says]: "Be rabbaniyyin [devoted to the Lord]"﴾ ... i.e., he says: be teachers of the people through your knowledge and your study. Teach the people and make things clear to them. Likewise the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say to the Jews, because they were People of the Book who know what the Arabs do not know.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 80:

﴿And He would not order you to take the angels and the prophets as lords.﴾ As the Christians and the Sabians did. ﴿Would He order you to disbelieve﴾ — an interrogative whose meaning is denial, i.e., He would not do that. ﴿After you have submitted [to Allah]?﴾ After your Islam.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 81:

﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets: "Whatever I have given you of the Book"﴾ Mā here is conditional, and the meaning is: "If I give you anything of the Book and wisdom, and whatever I give you," ﴿then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you will surely believe in him﴾. He means by the covenant of the Prophets their pledge that they would bear witness for Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this is His saying: ﴿Then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you﴾, meaning Muhammad, ﴿you shall surely believe in him and surely support him﴾. That is: if you encounter him; and Allah did not send any prophet except that He took from him the covenant concerning Muhammad (peace be upon him), and commanded him to take the covenant from his people that they would surely believe in him, and if he was sent while they were still alive, they would surely support him. This is an argument against the Jews. His saying: ﴿Do you affirm?﴾ means: Allah said to the Prophets: "Do you affirm belief in him and support for him?" ﴿And do you accept My burden upon that?﴾ means: "Have you accepted My covenant?" ﴿They said: "We affirm." He said: "Then bear witness."﴾ That is: against yourselves and against your followers, ﴿and I am with you among the witnesses﴾ over you and over them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 82:

﴿Then whoever turns away after that﴾ — i.e., turns away from it, after the covenant was taken and the signs of the Prophet (ﷺ) became manifest; ﴿those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾ — i.e., those who have gone out of faith.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 83:

﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah?﴾ After the covenant was taken from them to affirm belief in Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿While to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly﴾: the angels and the Muslims (willingly), and the disbelievers (unwillingly) at the time of severity. ﴿And to Him they will be returned﴾: a warning to them. That is: Do they seek other than the religion of Allah when they will be returned to Him?

﴿Say: "We believe in Allah"﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to say: "We believe in Allah and in all the messengers, without distinguishing between them in faith, as the Jews and the Christians did." A verse similar to this one has already been mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 86:

﴿How can Allah guide﴾ This is an interrogative with the sense of denial, meaning: Allah does not guide ﴿a people who disbelieved after their belief﴾. That is, the Jews were believers in Muhammad (ﷺ) before his mission; then when he was sent, they disbelieved in him. And His saying: ﴿and had testified﴾ means: after they had testified ﴿that the Messenger is true, and clear proofs had come to them﴾, meaning what was made clear in the Torah. ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ means: He does not guide those who broke the covenants of Allah, wronging themselves.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 87:

﴿Those—their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah﴾. A verse similar to this was mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 89:

﴿Except those who repent after that﴾, i.e., return to belief in Allah and affirmation of His Prophet, ﴿and reform﴾ their deeds.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 90:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief﴾ — they are the Jews — ﴿and then increased in disbelief﴾ — by persisting in their disbelief — ﴿their repentance will never be accepted﴾ — because they only repent at the moment of death's arrival, and that repentance is not accepted.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 91:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold﴾ — that is, the amount that would fill it. He says: If he were to ransom himself from the punishment with the earth filled with gold, it would not be accepted from him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 92:

﴿You will never attain righteousness﴾ (al-birr), i.e., piety (al-taqwa). It is also said: it means Paradise. ﴿until you spend from what you love﴾, i.e., you give out the zakat of your wealth.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 93:

﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel﴾, meaning: permissible, ﴿except what Israel had forbidden to himself before the Torah was revealed﴾. This is because Ya'qub (peace be upon him) fell gravely ill, and he vowed that if Allah, exalted is He, granted him recovery, he would forbid himself the food and drink he loved most. The food and drink he loved most were the meat of camels and their milk. When the Prophet (ﷺ) claimed that he knew the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the Jews said: "How can that be, when you eat the meat of camels and their milk?" The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "That was lawful for Ibrahim (peace be upon him)." The Jews then claimed that it had been forbidden to him. So Allah, exalted is He, revealed a refutation of them, and made clear that the origin of this prohibition was not in the Torah but was before its revelation, and this is His saying: ﴿Before the Torah was revealed. Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful﴾, the verse.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 94:

﴿Whoever then fabricates a lie against Allah﴾, that is: by attributing this prohibition to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, upon Ibrahim (Abraham) in the Torah, ﴿after that﴾, after the proof has become manifest that the prohibition was only from the side of Ya'qub (Jacob), peace be upon him, ﴿those are the wrongdoers﴾ against themselves.
﴿Say: "Allah has spoken the truth."﴾ In this and in all that He has informed of.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 96:

﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind﴾ is the one visited for pilgrimage (yuhajju ilayhi), ﴿is the one at Bakkah﴾, that is Makkah, ﴿blessed﴾, abounding in good, in that blessing was placed in it and with it, ﴿and guidance﴾, and possessing guidance, ﴿for the worlds﴾, because it is the qiblah of their prayers and an indication toward Allah through the signs He placed with it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 97:

﴿Therein are clear signs﴾ meaning: the sacred places (al-mashi'r) and the rites (al-manasik), all of them. Then he mentioned some of them, saying: ﴿the Station of Ibrahim (maqam Ibrahim)﴾, meaning: among them is the Station of Ibrahim. ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾, meaning: whoever performs the pilgrimage (hajj) and enters it is safe from the sins he had committed before that. It was also said: safe from the Fire. ﴿And due to Allah from the people is the pilgrimage to the House﴾. He stated the obligation in general terms, then specified it, using a substitution from "the people," saying ﴿for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾, meaning: whoever is strong in himself, so that hardship does not befall him in being at ease, and whoever has this attribute and possesses provision and a mount, the pilgrimage becomes obligatory for him. ﴿And whoever disbelieves﴾, meaning: denies the obligation of the pilgrimage, ﴿then indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 99:

﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, why do you hinder from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked, while you are witnesses?"﴾ Their hindering from the way of Allah was by denying the Prophet (ﷺ) and claiming that his description is not in their scripture. ﴿Seeking to make it crooked﴾ means you seek to make it crooked with the doubts that you dress up before your lowly ones. ﴿While you are witnesses﴾ to what is in the Torah, that the religion of Allah is Islam.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 100:

﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a group from those who were given the Scripture﴾ The verse was revealed concerning the Aws and the Khazraj, when some people from the Jews incited enmity between them in order to lead them astray from their religion. Then He addressed them, saying:
How can you disbelieve, when the signs of Allah, which indicate His oneness, are recited to you, and His Messenger is among you? And whoever holds fast to Allah, [i.e., believes in Allah].

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 102:

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah with the proper fear of Him﴾. It means: that He is obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not denied. When this was revealed, the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Who is able to do this?" It weighed heavily upon them, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾. The first [verse] was abrogated (naskh) by it. ﴿And do not die except while you are Muslims﴾, i.e., remain upon Islam until death comes to you and finds you upon it. In reality, it is a prohibition against abandoning Islam.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 103:

﴿And hold fast, all of you, to the rope of Allah﴾, that is: adhere to the religion of Allah. The address is to al-Aws and al-Khazraj. ﴿And do not be divided﴾ as you were in the pre-Islamic age, fighting one another over other than the religion of Allah. ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾ by means of Islam, ﴿when you were enemies﴾, meaning: the war that was between al-Aws and al-Khazraj, until Allah joined their hearts through Islam, so those enmities departed and they became brothers, loving one another. This is His saying: ﴿And He brought their hearts together, and by His favour you became brothers. And you were on the brink of a pit of the Fire, and He saved you from it﴾, that is: the edge of a pit of the Fire, had you died in the state you were in, ﴿and He saved you from it﴾, that is: delivered you from it, ﴿by Islam and by Muhammad (ﷺ)﴾. ﴿Thus﴾, that is: like this clarification recited to you, ﴿Allah makes clear to you His signs, that you may be guided﴾.
﴿And let there be among you a community﴾ etc. That is: let all of you be like that. The particle مِنْ (min) was used to specify the addressees, distinguishing them from others.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 105:

﴿And do not be like those who became divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them﴾ That is: the Jews and the Christians. That is: the Jews differed after Musa (Moses) and became sects, and likewise the Christians.

﴿On the Day when some faces will turn white﴾: that is, the faces of the Muhajirun (Emigrants), the Ansar (Helpers), and whoever believed in Muhammad (peace be upon him). ﴿And some faces will turn black﴾: the faces of the Jews and the Christians, and whoever disbelieved in him. ﴿As for those whose faces turned black﴾, it will be said to them: ﴿Did you disbelieve after your belief?﴾ Because they had testified to Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he was a prophet, but when he came to them they denied him and disbelieved in him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 107:

﴿As for those whose faces will be whitened, they will be in the mercy of Allah﴾ meaning: His Paradise.

﴿These are the signs of Allah﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿which We recite to you﴾, which We make clear, ﴿in truth﴾, with sincerity. ﴿And Allah does not desire injustice for the worlds﴾, so that He would punish them without any offence.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 110:

﴿You are the best nation﴾ with Allah, in the Preserved Tablet, meaning the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿brought forth for mankind﴾, made manifest to them. And Allah the Exalted has not brought forth for mankind a nation better than the nation of Muhammad (peace be upon him). Then He praised them for the qualities that were in them, saying: ﴿You enjoin what is right﴾, and the rest of the verse.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 111:

﴿They will not harm you﴾, that is, the Jews, ﴿except for a little harm﴾, meaning a minor harm by the tongue, such as threats and slander. ﴿And if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you﴾, defeated. God promised His Prophet and the believers victory over the Jews, and He fulfilled His promise, so the Jews of Medina never fought the Messenger of God (ﷺ) without being put to flight.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 112:

﴿Humiliation has been decreed upon them﴾, which we have mentioned, ﴿wherever they are found﴾, meaning wherever they are encountered and come upon, ﴿except with a rope from Allah﴾, meaning: but they may seek protection through a covenant (when they are given one), and the meaning is that they are abased in every place, except that they hold fast to a covenant (and the meaning is that they are abased in every place except that they hold fast to a covenant). What is intended by ﴿a rope from Allah and a rope from the people﴾ is the covenant, the protection (dhimmah), and the safe-conduct (aman) that they receive from the believers by the permission of Allah. The rest of the verse has been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah. Then He informed that they are not equal in their religion, so He said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 113:

﴿Not all of them are alike.﴾ He informs that among them are believers, saying: ﴿Among the People of the Book is a standing community﴾, i.e., upon the truth, ﴿reciting﴾, i.e., reading, ﴿the verses of Allah﴾, i.e., the Book of Allah, ﴿during the night hours﴾, i.e., its periods. He means ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and those who believed with him from the People of the Book. ﴿And they prostrate﴾, i.e., they pray.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 115:

﴿And whatever good they do, it will never be denied to them.﴾ You will not be denied its reward.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 116:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾ — the verse has already appeared at the beginning of this surah.

The commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 117:

﴿The likeness of what they spend in this worldly life﴾ means: the spending of the base among the Jews upon their scholars. ﴿Is like a wind in which is a freezing cold﴾, i.e. a severe cold, ﴿that has struck the tilth of a people who have wronged themselves﴾ through disbelief and disobedience. Allah the Exalted informs that the harm of their spending upon them is like the harm of this wind upon this crop. ﴿And Allah did not wrong them﴾, because everything He does to His creation is just on His part. ﴿But they wronged themselves﴾ through disbelief and disobedience. Then He forbade the believers from being intimate with them, so He said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 118:

﴿O you who have believed, do not take as biṭānah (intimates, confidants) ﴾ — meaning: dakhl (inner circle) and khawāṣṣ (close associates) — ﴿from other than yourselves﴾, i.e., from outside your religious community, ﴿they will not spare you corruption﴾ — meaning: they will not withhold their effort in harming you and corrupting you — ﴿they wish you would suffer﴾ — meaning: they wish for your going astray from your religion — ﴿hatred has already appeared﴾ — meaning: enmity has become manifest ﴿from their mouths﴾ through insult and slander against the Muslims, ﴿and what their breasts conceal is greater﴾ of enmity and treachery. ﴿We have already made the signs clear to you﴾ — meaning: the signs of the Jews in their enmity — ﴿if you use your reason﴾ — the place of benefit from the clarification.

﴿Here you are﴾: "ها" (*ha*) is an alerting particle (*tanbih*) that has entered upon "أنتم" (*antum*, "you"). ﴿Those﴾ ("أولاء", *ula'*) is in the sense of "الذين" (*alladhina*, "those who"), as if it were said: "those who ﴿love them but they do not love you﴾," meaning you wish Islam for them while they wish you to disbelieve. ﴿And you believe in the Book, all of it﴾, meaning in the books. "الكتاب" (*al-kitab*, "the Book") is an *ism jins* (a generic noun, one that denotes a whole category). ﴿And when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage﴾, meaning the tips of the fingers. The implied construction is: they bite the fingertips out of rage at you, and this is because of what they see of the unity of the believers and the cohesion of their word. ﴿Say: Die in your rage﴾: God Most High commanded His Prophet to invoke against them that their rage would persist until they die. ﴿Indeed God is All-Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾, of good and evil within them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 120:

﴿If good touches you﴾, that is victory and booty, ﴿it distresses them﴾, that is, it grieves them. ﴿And if evil befalls you﴾, the opposite of that, which is defeat and breaking, ﴿they rejoice at it. But if you are patient﴾ over what you hear of their harm, ﴿and fear Allah﴾, that is, avoid associating with them and mixing with them, ﴿their plotting will not harm you at all﴾, that is, their enmity. ﴿Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾, that is, knowing of it, so you will not lose its reward.

﴿And [remember] when you set out early from your family﴾, meaning: on the day of Uhud. ﴿From your family﴾ means from the dwelling of Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her). ﴿Preparing﴾ means arranging for the believers ﴿positions﴾, meaning stations and places ﴿for battle. And Allah is Hearing﴾ of what you say, ﴿Knowing﴾ of what is in your hearts.

﴿When two groups among you were about to lose heart﴾: Banu Salamah and Banu Harithah, ﴿to lose courage﴾: to become cowardly. This was because they had resolved to withdraw from the fighting, but Allah preserved them. ﴿And Allah is their protector﴾: their helper and ally. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾: let them depend on Him for sufficiency.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 123:

﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr, when you were humbled﴾, by your small number and your scarcity of weapons. ﴿So be mindful of Allah, that you may be grateful﴾. That is: so be mindful of Me, for that is the thanks for My blessing.
It is the day of Badr when you said to the believers: ﴿Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?﴾

Yes (بلى) is an affirmation of God's promise. ﴿If you are patient﴾ in facing the enemy, ﴿and fear God﴾ by avoiding disobedience to God and opposing the Prophet, peace be upon him, ( ﴿and they come upon you immediately﴾ it was said: from their direction, and it was said: from their anger). ﴿your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, marked﴾, meaning distinguished. The angels had been marked on the day of Badr with white wool on the forelocks and tails of the horses. Then the believers were patient on the day of Badr, so they were reinforced with five thousand angels.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 126:

﴿And Allah did not make it﴾, that is, that reinforcement, ﴿except as good news﴾, that is, as glad tidings for you, ﴿and that your hearts might be reassured thereby﴾, so that you would not despair at the multitude of the enemy. ﴿And victory is not from anyone but from Allah﴾, because whoever Allah does not help is forsaken, even if his supporters are many.

Translation of the passage:

﴿That He might cut off a band of those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., He granted you victory at Badr (ليقطع طرفاً أي:) so that He might demolish a pillar of the pillars of polytheism (shirk) through killing and capture, ﴿or disgrace them﴾, i.e., He humiliates them and abases them, meaning: those who were routed. His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 128:

﴿Thou hast no part in the affair﴾ (the verse). When the affair of Uhud came about, and what befell the polytheists happened, namely the breaking of the Prophet's (ﷺ) front tooth and the wounding of his face, he said: "How will a people prosper who have stained the face of their Prophet, while he is calling them to their Lord?!" So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, informing him that many of them would believe. The meaning: you have no say in the affair, regarding their punishment or their reform, until their repentance comes about or their punishment, and this is His saying: ﴿or He will turn to them in forgiveness or punish them﴾. So when He negated the affair from His Prophet (peace be upon him), He mentioned that the whole affair belongs to Him: whomever He wills He punishes, and whomever He wills He forgives, and this is His saying:

﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills﴾: that is, the great sin of those who affirm the Oneness of God (al-muwahhidin). ﴿And He punishes whom He wills﴾: he means the polytheists (al-mushrikin) for the small sin. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾ to His allies (awliya'ihi) ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 130:

﴿O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied﴾ [the verse]. That is: they used to add to the principal and postpone the term; whenever a term was deferred to another, an increase was added to the wealth.

﴿That you may be successful﴾: so that you may be felicitous and remain in Paradise.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 131:

﴿And guard yourselves against the Fire﴾ by forbidding usury and by abandoning the holding of it to be lawful, ﴿which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾, not for the believers.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 133:**

﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord﴾: that is, Islam, which necessitates forgiveness. It was also said: repentance. It was also said: the performance of the obligatory duties (al-fara'id). ﴿And a garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared﴾ for every one of the friends of God (awliya' Allah).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 134:

﴿Those who spend in ease and in hardship﴾ in prosperity and in adversity, in wealth and in its scarcity. ﴿And those who restrain their anger﴾ who hold back their rage from carrying it out. ﴿And who pardon people﴾ that is: the slaves (al-mamalik) and those who wronged them or mistreated them. ﴿And Allah loves the good-doers﴾ the monotheists who possess these qualities.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 135:

﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality﴾, i.e., fornication (zina), it was revealed concerning Nabhan al-Tammar (the date-seller). A beautiful woman came to him to buy dates from him, so he drew her to himself and kissed her. Then he regretted this, so he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and this verse was revealed. And His saying: ﴿or wrong themselves﴾, meaning: what falls short of fornication, such as a kiss, a touch, or a glance. ﴿They remember Allah﴾, i.e., they remember the punishment of Allah. ﴿And do not persist﴾, i.e., they do not insist or continue ﴿in what they have done﴾, but rather they acknowledge it and seek forgiveness. ﴿While they know﴾ that what they committed is forbidden and a sin.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 137:

﴿Indeed, there have passed before you [divine] ways (sunan)﴾ That is: there have passed from Me, concerning those nations before you that were disbelievers, ways (sunan) of respite I granted them, until they reach the term I set for their destruction. And there remain for them traces in this world, in which there is the greatest lesson. ﴿So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of﴾ the final outcome of ﴿those who denied﴾ among them. It was revealed concerning the story of the Day of Uhud. Allah says: I grant them respite until My appointed term arrives, by which I determined the victory of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his allies and the destruction of his enemies.

This is a clarification for mankind: that is, the Qur'an is a clarification for people in general, ﴿and guidance and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾, in particular, those whom God has guided by His bounty.

"Do not weaken"** (﴿ولا تهنوا﴾) — do not become feeble in fighting your enemy because of the defeat that befell you. **"Nor grieve"** (﴿ولا تحزنوا﴾) — that is, over what you lost of the spoils. **"You will be the superior ones"** (﴿وأنتم الأعلون﴾) — that is, for you the final outcome will be victory and triumph. **"If you are believers"** (﴿إن كنتم مؤمنين﴾) — that is, faith necessitates what has been mentioned: abandoning weakness and grief.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 140:

﴿If you have been touched by a wound﴾, that is, it afflicts you: wounds and their pain on the Day of Uhud. ﴿Then the people [the polytheists] have been touched by a wound like it﴾, on the Day of Badr. ﴿And those days﴾, that is, the days of this world, ﴿We alternate them﴾, We turn them ﴿among the people﴾: at one time in favour of one group, and at another time in favour of the other. ﴿And that Allah may know those who believe﴾, distinguished by faith from others. That is: We only give the victory to the disbelievers over the believers so that the sincere believer may be distinguished from the one who apostatises from the religion when a calamity befalls him. The meaning is: that He may know them as witnessed (mushahadatan) just as He knew them unseen (ghaiban). ﴿And that He may take from among you martyrs﴾, that is: to honour a people with martyrdom. ﴿And Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾, that is, the polytheists. That is: He only gives the polytheists power over the believers for the reasons mentioned, not because He loves them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 141:

﴿Wa-liyumahhisa Allahu alladhina amanu﴾ meaning: that He may purify them from their sins through what befalls them of killing, wounding and loss of property. ﴿Wa-yamhaqa al-kafirin﴾ meaning: He will utterly destroy them when He grants victory over them. That is: He grants victory over the believers for the reason mentioned, and He grants victory over the disbelievers so as to destroy them because of their sins.

Am ḥasibtum ﴿Am ḥasibtum﴾ — rather, "Did you suppose?" meaning: do not suppose ﴿that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those who strive (among you) and made evident the patient﴾, that is: and the knowledge (ʿilm) of jihad has not yet come about along with the knowledge of the patience of the patient ones. The verse is an address to those who fled on the Day of Uhud. It was said to them: "Did you suppose that you would enter Paradise as those who were killed entered it, and that you would stand firm under the pain of wounds and blows, without following their path and showing their patience?!"

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 143:

﴿And you had certainly been wishing for death﴾ They used to wish, on a day with the Prophet ﷺ, and they would say: "We will certainly do such-and-such, and we will certainly do such-and-such." Then they fled on the day of Uhud, and so they deserved the punishment. And His saying: ﴿before you encountered it﴾ means: before the day of Uhud. ﴿Then you have seen it﴾ you saw what you had been wishing for of death, that is, you saw its causes, but you did not stand firm with your Prophet. It was revealed as a rebuke from the Messenger to them, and they said: "We were told that you had been killed, and for that reason we fled." ﴿while you were looking on﴾ while you were clear-sighted, considering the situation and how it was, so why did you flee?

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 144:

﴿And Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him.﴾ That is: he will die just as the messengers before him died. ﴿So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?﴾ That is: will you apostatise into disbelief after your faith? This was when news spread at the Battle of Uhud that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been killed. Some people of the hypocrites (al-nifaq) said to the believers: "If Muhammad has been killed, then return to your former religion." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse: ﴿And whoever turns back on his heels, he will not harm Allah at all.﴾ That is: he only harms himself by earning punishment. ﴿And Allah will reward the grateful﴾ with the reward they deserve, ﴿the obedient to Allah among the Emigrants and the Helpers.⁠﴾ Then he rebuked those who had fled in defeat, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 145:

﴿And it is not for a soul to die except by the permission of Allah﴾, i.e., no soul would die except by the permission of Allah, by His decree and His measure. Allah has written that as "a decree with a specified term," until its appointed time that has been determined for it. So why did you flee? Flight does not add to one's life. ﴿And whoever desires the reward of this world﴾ by his deeds and obedience, ﴿We give him of it﴾ — We give him from it what We have decreed for him. That is, for these fleeing ones who sought the spoils of war. ﴿And whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter﴾ — meaning those who stood firm until they were killed — ﴿We give him of it.﴾ Then he argued against the fleeing ones with His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 146:

﴿Wa-ka-ayyin﴾ meaning: and how many (wa-kam). ﴿Min nabiyyin qatala﴾ (how many a prophet fought) in a battle, ﴿ma‘ahu ribbiyyuna kathir﴾ (with him were many groups of devoted worshippers), ﴿fa-ma wahanu li-ma asabahum﴾ meaning: they did not weaken after what befell them, namely the killing of their prophet, the verse...

{Wa-ma kana qawluhum} — "And their saying was not," that is, the saying of the companions of that prophet who was killed in battle after the killing of their prophet, {illa an qalu rabbana ighfir lana dhunubana wa-israfana} — "except that they said: Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses," meaning our going beyond the limits set for us, {fi amrina wa-thabbit aqdamana} — "in our affair, and make firm our feet," with strength from You and victory.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 148:

﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world﴾ victory and triumph; ﴿and the good reward of the Hereafter﴾ the recompense and forgiveness.

O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve (ﷺ... no) — 

Translation:

﴿O you who believe, if you obey those who disbelieve﴾ — that is, the Jews and the polytheists, when they said to you on the day of Uhud: "Return to the religion of your forefathers." This is His saying: ﴿they will turn you back on your heels﴾ — they will make you return to your original state of polytheism (shirk) with Allah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 150:

﴿Rather, Allah is your Protector﴾. That is: so be independent of allying yourselves with the disbelievers, for I am your Helper, so do not seek help from them. When the polytheists turned away from Uhud, they resolved to return in order to uproot the Muslims, and the Muslims feared that. So Allah the Exalted promised them the forsaking of their enemies, by His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 151:

﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾: fear, so that they will not return against you. ﴿Because they associated with Allah﴾: that is, because of their associating others with Allah ﴿that for which He had sent down no authority﴾: no proof or evidence; that is, the idols they worship alongside Allah without any proof. ﴿And their refuge is the Fire﴾: that is, their place of return is the Fire. ﴿And wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers﴾: their dwelling place.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 152:

﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you﴾ with victory and triumph, ﴿when you were killing them﴾, that is, killing the polytheists on the Day of Uhud at the beginning of the matter, ﴿by His permission﴾, by Allah's knowledge and will, ﴿until, when you lost courage﴾, that is, you became cowardly toward your enemy, ﴿and disputed⁠﴾, that is, differed about the matter, meaning: some of them said, "What is the point of our standing here, when the disbelieving folk have been routed?" and some of them said, "We will not go beyond the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." This disagreement took place among the archers who were at the position (al-markaz), ﴿and disobeyed⁠﴾ the Messenger by abandoning the position, ﴿after He had shown you what you love⁠﴾, namely victory and triumph over your enemies. ﴿Among you are those who desire this world⁠﴾, and they are the ones who left the position and turned toward the booty (al-dhahab), ﴿and among you are those who desire the Hereafter⁠﴾, that is, those who remained steadfast at the position. ﴿Then He turned you away from them⁠﴾, that is, He turned you back in defeat ﴿from the disbelievers⁠﴾, ﴿so that He might test you⁠﴾, that is, to examine you by what He had imposed upon you of reversal (al-dabra), so that the patient would be distinguished from the impatient and the sincere from the hypocrite. ﴿And He has certainly pardoned you⁠﴾ for your sin of disobeying the Prophet (ﷺ) and for the defeat, ﴿and Allah is full of bounty toward the believers⁠﴾ through forgiveness.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 153:

﴿When you were climbing up﴾ going far off in flight, ﴿and not turning [back] for anyone﴾ not stopping for anyone, ﴿while the Messenger was calling you from behind you﴾ from after you, saying: "To me, servants of Allah! (To me, servants of Allah! To me, servants of Allah!)" and you were not turning toward him. ﴿So He rewarded you﴾ meaning: He replaced what you had returned of reward with ﴿grief﴾, which is the grief of the defeat and the victory of the polytheists, ﴿for a grief﴾ meaning: for your grief caused to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when you disobeyed him, ﴿so that you would not grieve﴾ meaning: He pardoned you so that you would not grieve ﴿over what had escaped you﴾ of the spoils of war ﴿nor for what had befallen you﴾ of killing and wounds.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 154:

﴿Then He sent down upon you, after the distress, security in the form of drowsiness (amanatan nu'asan)﴾ This was because they feared a renewed attack by the polytheists upon them, and they were under the shields (al-hajaf), ready for battle. So God the Exalted granted them a security in which they could sleep. This was specific to the believers, and it is His saying: ﴿Some of you were overcome by drowsiness, while others were concerned for themselves﴾. These were the hypocrites (al-munafiqun), whose only concern was the salvation of their own souls. ﴿They harbor thoughts about God that are not true﴾, i.e., they thought that the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ) had collapsed and that he would not be helped. ﴿Thoughts of the period of ignorance (zann al-jahiliyyah)﴾, i.e., like the thoughts of the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah), who were the disbelievers. ﴿They say: "Do we have any say in the affair at all?"﴾ meaning: we have no share in victory and triumph, as we were promised. They say this in denial. So God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the affair is entirely with God﴾, i.e., victory, martyrdom, destiny and decree. ﴿They conceal within themselves﴾ of doubt and hypocrisy ﴿what they do not reveal to you. They say: "If we had any say in the affair, we would not have been killed here."﴾ meaning: they were taken out unwillingly, and if the matter had been in their hands they would not have gone out. This is a denial of divine decree on their part, so God replied to them with His saying: ﴿Say: "Even if you had been in your houses, those destined to be killed would have come forth to their places of death (madaji'ihim)"﴾, i.e., their places of falling.
