Their staying behind would not have saved them. ﴿And that God might test what is in your breasts﴾, O hypocrites, ﴿and that He might purify what is in your hearts﴾, O believers, ﴿and God is Knower of what is in the breasts﴾, i.e., its inner contents.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 155:

﴿Indeed, those of you who turned away﴾, O believers, ﴿on the day the two hosts met﴾, that is, those who fled on the day of Uhud. ﴿It was only Satan who caused them to slip﴾, that is, drove them into error, ﴿because of some of what they had earned﴾, meaning, because of their disobedience to the Prophet (ﷺ) in abandoning the post. ﴿And Allah has already pardoned them﴾ for that sin.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 156:

﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved﴾, that is, the hypocrites, ﴿and said of their brothers﴾, that is, concerning their brothers by lineage, ﴿when they traveled through the land﴾, that is, journeyed and then died or perished, ﴿or were [engaged in] raiding﴾, plural of ghazin (one who raids), and were killed. ﴿Had they remained with us, they would not have died or been killed﴾, denying the decree and divine predestination. ﴿So that Allah may make that a regret in their hearts﴾, that is, so that their assumption that had they not attended the battle, death would have been averted from them becomes a regret in their hearts. ﴿A regret in their hearts﴾: He forbids the believers from being like these disbelievers in this statement of theirs, so that Allah may make that a regret in their hearts and not in the hearts of the believers. ﴿And Allah gives life and causes death﴾, so a person's caution cannot prevent him from meeting his appointed term.

﴿And if you are killed﴾, that is: By Allah, if you are killed ﴿in the cause of Allah﴾, in jihad, O believers, ﴿or die﴾ in the cause of Allah, ﴿you will surely be forgiven by Him and shown mercy, and that is ﴾better than what they accumulate﴿, from the goods of this world.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 158:

﴿And if you die﴾ while remaining steadfast in jihad, ﴿or are killed﴾ as fighters in the way of God, ﴿to God you will indeed be gathered﴾ in either case.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 159:

﴿Then by mercy from Allah﴾ That is: by mercy, i.e., by blessing from Allah and His kindness toward you. ﴿You were gentle with them﴾ O Muhammad, i.e., your character was made gentle toward them and your forbearance was great. ﴿And had you been harsh﴾ coarse in speech ﴿and hard-hearted﴾ in deed ﴿they would have scattered﴾ dispersed ﴿from around you. So pardon them﴾ for what they did on the Day of Uhud ﴿and ask forgiveness for them﴾ so that I may intercede for them ﴿and consult them in the matter﴾ to console their hearts and raise their standing, and so that it becomes a sunnah ﴿And when you have decided﴾ upon what you wish to carry out ﴿then rely upon Allah﴾ not upon the consultation.

﴿If Allah helps you, none can overcome you﴾ from among the people, ﴿and if He forsakes you﴾ (on the day of Uhud), then none can help you after Him. The meaning: Do not abandon My command for the sake of the people, and renounce the people for the sake of My command.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 161:

﴿And it is not for a prophet to defraud﴾ i.e., to betray by concealing something of the war booty from his companions. It was revealed concerning a red woolen cloak that was lost on the day of Badr, and the people said: "Perhaps the Prophet (ﷺ) took it." So Allah, exalted is He, negated misappropriation (ghulul) from him and made clear that no prophet ever misappropriated; the meaning is: it is not for a prophet to commit ghulul. ﴿And whoever defrauds will bring what he defrauded on the Day of Resurrection, carrying it upon his back.﴾ ﴿Then every soul will be paid in full what it has earned﴾ i.e., it will be recompensed for the reward of its deeds. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ — they will not be diminished anything from the reward of their deeds.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on Surah 3, verse 162:

﴿Is then one who pursues the pleasure of Allah﴾ by believing in Him and obeying Him, meaning: the believers, ﴿like one who has incurred the wrath of Allah﴾ by disbelieving in Him and disobeying Him, meaning: the hypocrites.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 163:

﴿They are ranks with Allah﴾ That is: they are people of different ranks with Allah, meaning that they differ in their standings. For those who follow the good pleasure of Allah there is honour and reward, and for those who return with wrath from Allah there is humiliation and punishment. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾ In this is an exhortation to obedience and a warning against disobedience.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 164:

﴿Indeed, Allah conferred a favour upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves﴾. That is: one of them, whose affair was known, and whose report of truthfulness and trustworthiness was known, not an angel, nor anyone other than the descendants of Adam. The rest of the verse has been mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah. ﴿And indeed they had been before that﴾, and they had been before his sending, ﴿in clear error﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 165:

﴿Or when a calamity struck you﴾: that is, when a calamity struck you, meaning what befell them on the Day of Uhud, ﴿though you had inflicted twice as much﴾ (on them) on the Day of Badr. That is because they killed seventy and took seventy captives, and seventy of them were killed on the Day of Uhud. ﴿You said, "How is this?"﴾ From where has this killing and defeat reached us, when we are Muslims and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is among us? ﴿Say, "It is from yourselves."﴾ That is: you abandoned your position and sought booty, so the evil came to you from your own side. ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ to grant victory when you obey your Prophet, and to withhold it when you oppose him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 166:

﴿And whatever befell you on the day the two hosts met﴾ — the day of Uhud — ﴿was by the permission of Allah﴾ — by His decree and His predestination; He is consoling them with this. ﴿And that He might make evident the believers﴾ — steadfast and patient — ﴿and that He might make evident the hypocrites﴾ — distressed by what befell them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 167:

﴿And it was said to them﴾ to ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions when they turned away from the believers that day, ﴿"Come, fight in the way of Allah, or repel [the enemy]"﴾ from us, by increasing our numbers, if you will not fight. ﴿They said, "Had we known there would be fighting, we would certainly have followed you."﴾ That is: if we knew that you would be fighting today, we would have followed you, but there will be no fighting today. They said this as hypocrites, because had they known that, they would not have followed them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith﴾ by what they displayed of forsaking the believers, ﴿nearer to disbelief than to faith﴾ because they had been nearer to faith before that by their outward condition; but when they forsook the believers, they became nearer to disbelief in terms of the outward.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 168:

﴿Those who said﴾ — that is, the hypocrites — ﴿to their brothers﴾ — to their like among the people of hypocrisy — ﴿and stayed behind﴾ — from the struggle (jihad). The waw here is for the circumstantial clause (al-hal). ﴿If they had obeyed us﴾ — they mean the martyrs of Uhud — in withdrawing from the Prophet ﷺ and remaining behind, ﴿they would not have been killed.﴾ So God, exalted is He, responded to them and said: ﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad, ﴿Then avert﴾ — push away, ﴿ward off from yourselves death, if you are truthful﴾ — if you are truthful that caution averts what has been decreed (al-qadar).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 169:

﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ — meaning: the martyrs of Uhud. ﴿Rather, they are alive with their Lord﴾: rather, they are alive ﴿with their Lord﴾ in the abode of His honour, because their souls are in the crops of green birds. ﴿Being provided for﴾: they eat.

(Fariheen) joyful, rejoicing ﴿in what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾, ﴿and they receive good tidings regarding those who have not yet joined them from behind them﴾, meaning: they rejoice over their brothers whom they left behind, hoping for them martyrdom, so that they may attain the like of what they have attained. ﴿That there is no fear upon them﴾, i.e., that there is no fear upon them, meaning: upon their believing brothers when they join them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 172:

﴿Those who answered the call of Allah and the Messenger﴾ — they responded to them both, ﴿after the wound had struck them﴾, i.e., the injuries, ﴿for those among them who did good﴾ by obeying the Messenger and guarding against opposing him, ﴿there is a great reward.﴾ It was revealed concerning those who obeyed the Messenger when he summoned them to go out in pursuit of Abu Sufyan on the day of Uhud, when Abu Sufyan had resolved to turn back toward Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions to annihilate them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 173:

﴿Those to whom the people said﴾ (the verse). Abu Sufyan had promised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he would meet him at Badr al-Sughra (the Lesser Badr) the following year, from the day of Uhud. When the following year came, he sent Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud al-Ashja'i to frighten the believers away from meeting him. This is what is meant by His words:

﴿Those﴾, meaning: the believers. ﴿To whom the people said﴾, meaning: Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud. ﴿Indeed, the people﴾, meaning: Abu Sufyan and his companions, ﴿have gathered against you﴾, with the caravan of perfume (al-latimah), the market of Makkah. ﴿So fear them﴾, and do not go out to them. ﴿But that increased them in faith﴾, that statement, ﴿in faith﴾, meaning: steadfastness in their religion and perseverance in supporting their Prophet. ﴿And they said, "Sufficient for us is Allah"﴾, meaning: the one who suffices us in their affair is Allah. ﴿And He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾, meaning: the one to whom the matter is entrusted.

So they returned with a blessing from Allah and bounty (ربح, profit). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to that appointment, but he did not meet anyone from the polytheists, and they arrived at the market, for it was a market place of theirs. So they traded and made a profit, and returned to Madinah safe and victorious. This is His saying: ﴿They were not touched by any harm﴾, that is, no killing and no wounds, ﴿and they followed the pleasure of Allah﴾ to Badr al-Sughra (Badr the Lesser), in obedience to Him and obedience to His Messenger. His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 175:

﴿It is only Satan who frightens you of his allies﴾. That is: he frightens you with his allies, meaning the disbelievers. ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me﴾ in abandoning My command ﴿if you are believers﴾, affirming My promise.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 176:

﴿And do not let those who hasten to disbelief grieve you.﴾ That is: in supporting it (kufr), and they are the hypocrites (munafiqun), the Jews (Yahud), and the polytheists (mushrikun). ﴿Indeed, they will not harm Allah﴾ That is: His allies (awliya') and His religion (din) ﴿at all.﴾ Rather, the consequence of that returns upon them. ﴿Allah intends not to give them a share (hazz)﴾ a portion (nasib) ﴿in the Hereafter﴾ in Paradise (al-Jannah).

﴿Indeed, those who have exchanged disbelief for faith﴾, i.e., they replaced [faith with disbelief]. Repeated: ﴿they will never harm Allah in the least﴾. He mentioned it in the first place as a cause (ʿilla) for the consolation (tasliyah) that is due regarding their hastening into misguidance, and He mentioned it in the second place as a cause for the harm being specific to the one who disobeys, not to the one who is disobeyed.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 178:

﴿Let not those who disbelieve suppose that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite that they may increase in sin.﴾ That is: that Our granting them respite, which is delay and postponement, is good for their souls. ﴿We only give them respite that they may increase in sin.﴾ That is: We lengthen their lives so that they may increase in sin, because of their obstinacy against the truth and their opposition to the Messenger. The verse was revealed concerning a people among the disbelievers whom God, exalted is He, knew would never believe, and that their remaining alive would only increase them in disbelief.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 179:

﴿God would not leave the believers in the state you are in﴾, O believers, from the mixing of the hypocrite with the believer, ﴿until He distinguishes the wicked from the good﴾, that is, the hypocrite from the believer. He did that on the day of Uhud, because the hypocrites had shown their hypocrisy by their withdrawal. ﴿Nor would God disclose to you the unseen﴾, so that you might recognise the hypocrite from the believer before the distinguishing. ﴿But God﴾ chooses for knowing that whomever He wills from among the messengers, and Muhammad was among those whom God chose for this knowledge.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 180:

﴿Let not those who withhold⁠ ﴾ — that is: let not those who are stingy ﴿with what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾ (i.e., of wealth) ⁠— with that which is obligatory in it, the zakat — think… This was revealed concerning those who withhold zakat. ﴿It is better for them﴾ — that is: withholding is better for them. ﴿Rather, it is worse for them.﴾ Because by it they deserve the punishment of Allah. ﴿They will have their necks encircled with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ That is: the wealth they withheld will be made into a serpent, which will encircle their necks and bite them from their horn to their foot. ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth.﴾ That is: He will cause its people to perish, and the possessions and wealth will remain for Allah, and there is no owner of them except Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 181:

﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich."﴾ It was revealed concerning the Jews when they said, after the revelation of His words, ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan?﴾: "Indeed, Allah is poor and asks us for a loan, and we are rich. If He were rich, He would not have borrowed our wealth." ﴿We will record what they have said﴾, i.e., We will command the recording angels (al-hafaza) to inscribe that in their records of deeds. The verse (al-ayah).

﴿That﴾ i.e., that punishment, ﴿is for what your hands have sent forward﴾ for what you previously committed of crimes, ﴿and that Allah﴾ and that Allah ﴿is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ so as to punish them without any crime.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 183:

﴿Those who said, "Indeed, Allah has taken a covenant from us﴾ — i.e., the Jews. This is because the command concerning the Children of Israel in the Torah was that they should not believe in any messenger who came to them until he brought them a sacrifice that fire would consume, except for the Messiah and Muhammad, peace be upon them both. So they would say to Muhammad, peace be upon him: "We will not believe you until you bring us a sacrifice that fire consumes, for Allah has made that covenant with us." So Allah the Exalted said to Muhammad, peace be upon him, as an establishment of the proof against them: ﴿Say, "There have already come to you messengers before me﴾ ... Then the Prophet ﷺ consoled himself regarding their denial with His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 184:

﴿If they deny you, then messengers before you were denied, who came with the clear proofs and the scriptures and the illuminating Book﴾ — i.e., the scriptures; ﴿and the illuminating Book﴾ — i.e., the guiding one to the truth.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 185:

﴿Every soul shall taste death, and you will only be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection. So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed triumphed.﴾ That is: he has attained good and been saved from evil. ﴿And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.﴾ That is: living in this transient abode. ﴿Nothing but the enjoyment of delusion﴾ because it deceives a person with what it promises him of long life, while it comes to an end soon.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 186:

﴿Surely you will be tested﴾ (la-tublawunna): you, O believers, will be tested ﴿in your wealth﴾ through the obligations concerning it, ﴿and in your selves﴾ through prayer, fasting, the Hajj and jihad. ﴿And you will surely hear much hurt from those who were given the Book﴾, namely the Jews, ﴿and from those who associate partners with God﴾, namely the polytheists, ﴿much hurt﴾ through insult and reproach. ﴿But if you endure﴾ that hurt by refraining from retaliation, ﴿indeed that is of the steadfast resolve of affairs﴾, meaning it is among the true realities of faith.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 187:

﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture﴾ Allah took the covenant of the Jews in the Torah that they would make clear the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ), his description, and his sending, and that they would not conceal it. But they cast the covenant behind their backs and did not act by it. This is His saying: ﴿But they cast it behind their backs and bartered it for a small price﴾, i.e., what they used to take from their inferior folk through their leadership in knowledge. ﴿How evil is what they barter﴾: their bartering was abhorrent, and they incurred loss.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 188:

﴿Do not think that those who rejoice﴾ are the Jews, who rejoiced at misleading people and at people ascribing knowledge to them, though they are not such, and they loved to be praised for adhering to the truth, and they said: "We are the people of the Torah and the possessors of ancient knowledge." ﴿So do not think them to be in a place of safety﴾, that is, in deliverance ﴿from the punishment﴾.
﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾: i.e., He owns their management and their direction as He wills. The verse and the one after it were mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 191:

﴿Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides﴾ That is: they pray in these states, according to their ability. ﴿And reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, so that this increases their insight. ﴿"Our Lord"﴾ That is: they say, ﴿"Our Lord, You did not create this in vain"﴾, that is, this which we see of the creation of the heavens and the earth ﴿in vain﴾, that is, a creation without purpose; meaning: You created it as a proof of Your wisdom and the perfection of Your power.

Translation:

﴿Our Lord, indeed whomever You admit into the Fire, You have certainly disgraced⁠﴾ — meaning, to abide in it forever — ﴿and You have disgraced him﴾: that is, destroyed him and humiliated him. ﴿And for the wrongdoers﴾, that is, the disbelievers, ﴿there are no helpers﴾ who could protect them from the punishment of God.

Quranic quotations are in ﴿ ﴾ markers. Translate.

﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith﴾ That is: Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an. ﴿calling to faith﴾ means: calling to belief. ﴿"Believe in your Lord," so we believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds﴾ That is: cover and conceal our sins from us by accepting our acts of obedience, so that they become an expiation for them. ﴿And take us in death with the righteous﴾ meaning: the prophets; that is, among their number, so that we may be with them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 194:

﴿Our Lord, give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾, i.e., upon their tongues, of victory for us and humiliation for our enemies. ﴿And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection﴾, i.e., do not destroy us with punishment. saying
﴿Some of you are from others.﴾ That is: the ruling for all of you is the ruling for each one of you, regarding what I do with you in recompensing you for your deeds and not losing them for you.

﴿Do not let the movement of those who disbelieve throughout the land deceive you.﴾ Their going about for trade in the lands. The reason was that they used to trade and live in comfort in the lands, and some of the believers said: "The enemies of God are, as we see, in good state, while we have perished from hunger and hardship." So this verse was revealed.

Qawwah (strength; a reading of the word as given in the source).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 3, verse 197:

﴿A little enjoyment﴾. That is, that gain and profit is a little enjoyment, because it is transient and comes to an end.

Their provision: ﴿A provision﴾. The nuzul (nuzl) is what is prepared for a guest, and its meaning here is reward and recompense. ﴿And what is with God is better for the righteous﴾ than what the disbelievers enjoy in their comfortable turning about [in the land]. Then he mentioned the believers among the People of the Book, saying:

O you who have believed, be patient (ṣabr). That is: be patient upon your religion, and do not abandon it because of hardship that has befallen you. It was also said: upon jihad. ﴿And be steadfast (ṣābirū)﴾ against your enemy, so that they are not more steadfast than you. ﴿And stand guard (rābiṭū)﴾ — that is: persist in striving against your enemy, with war and with argument.
